description.narrative:
The Project targets the enhancement of wastewater treatment services in an area located northeast of Ramallah, in Palestine. A preparatory study for the Project, including a feasibility study and the preliminary environmental and social impact assessment (ESIA) was prepared with the Bank¿s own resources in 2019/2020. Detailed design and tender preparation services are funded by a World Bank grant and are currently under preparation. The Project will be implemented by the PWA. Activities under the Project will cover infrastructure investments and a technical assistance package.

The infrastructure investments will include the following main components: the construction of a wastewater collection system including trunk sewer lines and local networks, the construction of a wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) and the construction of reuse facilities for the utilisation of the treated effluent wastewater for agricultural and potentially other purposes.

The Project is expected to be executed in two phases (implemented in parallel), with a first phase covering the construction of the WWTP and related wastewater collection system, while the construction of reuse facilities will be added during the second phase.  The project is expected to be executed in two phases (that will be implemented in parallel), with a first phase covering the construction of the WWTP and related wastewater collection system (project cost of Phase 1: EUR 40m), while the reuse components shall be added during the Phase 2 (project cost of Phase 2: EUR 15m). All activities covered by both phases are expected to be implemented within the period between 2024-2028. Phase 1 of the project will be financed pari-passu and pro rata from the EIB loan and the EU NIP Investment Grants,to the extent possible.
